prompt.context_jp: 夜の帰り道、沙名子はふと立ち止まり…
prompt.prompt_jp: 夜の帰り道、沙名子___ふと立ち止まり、自分の胸に流れ込んでくる感情の重さを量っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits — Sanako is the ongoing topic of this narrative passage.

feedback.correct_en: は marks Sanako as the established topic the narration is tracking. The sentence is about what she, our familiar protagonist, is doing — not introducing her as new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame her as newly spotlighted information, as if the reader didn't already know whose evening walk this is. を doesn't fit a subject slot here.

contrast_examples.jp: 沙名子は立ち止まった。

prompt.context_jp: 太陽と沙名子の関係について
prompt.prompt_jp: 太陽の明るさ___、いつも沙名子から何かを引き出しては、返しきれない分だけを彼女の胸に残していく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle — the sentence sets up 'Taiyo's brightness' as the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 太陽の明るさ as the theme the sentence will unpack ('as for Taiyo's brightness, it always…'). The following clause gives a general characterization, which pairs naturally with topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read like a one-time event report rather than a general statement about what his brightness does. に is grammatically wrong here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の優しさは人を救う。
contrast_examples.en: His kindness (as a theme) saves people.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の優しさが急に出た。

prompt.prompt_jp: 社長の息子が専務として着任するという噂___、すでに社内を駆けめぐっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the big noun phrase as the topic of this sentence?

feedback.correct_en: は frames the long rumor-clause as the topic, then comments on it (it had already spread). This 'A は B' pattern is natural when the noun is already set up as what the sentence is about.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the rumor sound like brand-new, event-report information. を can't mark the subject of 駆けめぐる.

prompt.context_jp: 真夕がパソコンの画面を見て
prompt.prompt_jp: あっ！ 入札___ されてる！
prompt.prompt_en: Mayu just noticed something on screen. Pick the particle that marks the new, in-the-moment discovery.

feedback.correct_en: が flags newly-noticed information in an exclamation. Mayu is reacting to something she just saw, so が spotlights the bid as fresh info.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a known topic ('as for the bid…'), which clashes with the surprised 'あっ！'. に is wrong for the subject.

contrast_examples.en: The rain is falling (as for it).

prompt.context_jp: 専務が入ってくる場面
prompt.prompt_jp: 扉___開く瞬間、部屋の空気が一段と張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the subordinate clause describing a specific moment.

feedback.correct_en: In subordinate clauses like 〜する瞬間 the subject typically takes が, marking it as an event-level detail inside the modifier. The door opening is a specific, bounded occurrence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to make 扉 the sentence-wide topic, but the main-clause topic is really 部屋の空気. Subordinate-clause subjects strongly prefer が.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開く瞬間、彼は立った。
contrast_examples.en: The moment the door opened, he stood.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアは古かったが開いた。
contrast_examples.en: The door was old but opened.

prompt.prompt_jp: たくさんありそうですね 私の仕事___
prompt.prompt_en: Enjo surveys the paper piles and comments on his own job. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は presents 私の仕事 as the postposed topic ('…there's lots, I mean, my work'). It's an inversion where the comment comes first and the topic is clarified afterward.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mean 'my work' is the new, exhaustive answer to an unspoken question, which doesn't match this reflective tone. を can't mark the subject of ある.

contrast_examples.jp: 忙しそうですね、この部署は。
この部署が一番忙しい。

prompt.prompt_jp: 別に なんかしてもらいたいって 思ってるわけじゃないと思うけどね 山田太陽___
prompt.prompt_en: Mitsuki is specifically singling Taiyo out as the person who doesn't expect anything. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: は names 山田太陽 as the postposed topic ('…I don't think he wants anything — Taiyo, I mean'). It also carries a mild contrastive flavor: whatever other guys might want, Taiyo isn't like that.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into exhaustive-identification ('it's Taiyo who…'), which doesn't match Mitsuki's reassuring tone. も would mean 'Taiyo too', which contradicts the point.

prompt.context_jp: 専務が呼び止めたのは…
prompt.prompt_jp: 声をかけられたの___、先ほど楯突いた新入りだった。
prompt.prompt_en: The sentence identifies WHO got called out, among all the people in the room. Which particle fits a cleft-like identification?

feedback.correct_en: Actually は is the natural fit here: 〜のは…だった is the standard cleft pattern that presents the known action as topic and lets the predicate name the answer. The identified element (the newcomer) is the new info in the predicate, not before the particle.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a different structure and sound off. を doesn't fit a nominalized subject.

contrast_examples.en: The one who won is him.

prompt.prompt_jp: ないよ だって 私 なんのプラスにもなれてない
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako says she can't contribute anything positive. Pick the particle that gives '私' a contrastive/topic flavor ('as for me, unlike him, …').

feedback.correct_en: は on 私 contrasts her with Taiyo: he gives her a lot, but as for her, she can't give anything back. The whole chapter frames this imbalance explicitly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a plain subject identification without the self-contrast tone. も would imply 'me too', which doesn't fit a confession of inadequacy.

contrast_examples.jp: 私はできない（けど彼はできる）。

prompt.prompt_jp: 女___時に 優しさより 権力を選ぶんです
prompt.prompt_en: Chiaki makes a general statement about women. Which particle fits a generic topic?

feedback.correct_en: は marks 女 as a generic topic for a general-truth statement ('as for women, they sometimes…'). Gnomic/characterizing claims about a whole category typically use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as event-report ('a woman chose…'), not a generalization. を can't mark the subject.

prompt.prompt_jp: ムダだと思うけどな 数字で動く人間___ 数字でしか動かせない
prompt.prompt_en: Takakura characterizes a type of person. Which particle marks the generic topic?

feedback.correct_en: は presents '数字で動く人間' as the generic category being described. Characterizing statements about a kind of person naturally use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single out specific individuals as new info, which doesn't match this proverb-like observation. に changes the role entirely.

prompt.prompt_jp: 新参の麻吹美華は、机の上の書類___きちんとそろえながら、耳をそばだてている。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking the direct object of そろえる.

feedback.correct_en: そろえる is a transitive verb and 書類 is what she is arranging — the direct object slot takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and は are subject-marking particles and don't fit the object role here, especially with the overt subject 麻吹美華は already set.

prompt.prompt_jp: 会社の屋上___上がった鎌本は、風に前髪を揺らしながら…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the destination of 上がる.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the goal/destination of a motion verb like 上がる — 'went up to the rooftop'.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location where an action takes place, not where you move to. を would mark a path traversed (as in 道を歩く), which doesn't fit 上がる here.

prompt.prompt_jp: 希梨香の作ったサンプルを目にした樹菜は、その場で目___輝かせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle in this idiomatic expression 'eyes sparkled'.

feedback.correct_en: 目を輝かせる is a transitive set phrase — the person causes their eyes to shine, so 目 takes を. The subject (樹菜) is already marked with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目が輝く exists but is intransitive ('eyes shine on their own'), and would clash with the causative form 輝かせた here.

contrast_examples.en: The child made her eyes light up.

prompt.prompt_jp: 新発田は一同を叱咤して席___着かせ、机の上の菓子や飲み物にまで気を使って隠させた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 席 with 着く (to take a seat).

feedback.correct_en: 席に着く is the fixed combination: に marks the seat as the destination/endpoint of sitting. Even in the causative 着かせる, this particle stays に.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would try to make 席 a direct object, but 着く is intransitive. で would mark a location of activity, not the seat you settle into.

prompt.prompt_jp: 私 見ちゃったんだけど なんなの？ ___
prompt.prompt_en: Mitsuki tells Sanako what to say. In 私___見ちゃった, which particle fits a confession/contrast ('I, for one, saw it')?

feedback.correct_en: は on 私 sets the speaker up as the topic of a mini-statement with a slight contrastive edge: 'I saw it (whatever he thinks).' This fits Mitsuki's suggested confrontation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 私 feel like exhaustive identification ('I'm the one who saw') which is overly emphatic. を is wrong for the subject.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who saw it.

prompt.prompt_jp: 彼にとって、数字に現れないもの___すべて不要なものだった。
prompt.prompt_en: The sentence describes Enjo's worldview in general. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks '数字に現れないもの' as the general topic being characterized — 'as for things not shown by numbers, they are all unnecessary.' Characterizing a whole category this way takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single out one specific thing as new info, which doesn't match the sweeping judgment. を can't fit a copula-predicate subject here.

contrast_examples.en: Things you can't see are scary (in general).

prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子はその不釣り合いを、心の奥でひそかに帳簿に___ていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that fits the accounting metaphor 'kept a ledger of imbalance in her heart'.

feedback.correct_en: 帳簿につける is the set collocation for 'to record/enter into a ledger'. It perfectly fits Sanako the accountant mentally bookkeeping her emotional debt.
feedback.incorrect_en: 書く is too general — you'd say 帳簿に書く only rarely. 数える means 'count', not record.

prompt.prompt_jp: 太陽はいやな予感を覚えつつ、しぶしぶ___を貸すしかなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the body-part noun that completes the idiom for 'reluctantly listening'.

feedback.correct_en: 耳を貸す literally 'to lend one's ear' is the fixed idiom meaning 'to listen to someone'. It fits Taiyo being dragged into Kamamoto's story.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目を貸す isn't an idiom. 手を貸す means 'to lend a hand/help', which is about physical assistance, not listening.

contrast_examples.en: Lend me your ear for a sec.

prompt.context_jp: 円城がノベルティを手にして
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼はそれを手に取り、___するように眺めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word matching Enjo's cold, appraising gaze at the sample bag.

feedback.correct_en: 値踏み means 'to appraise/size up the worth of something', fitting Enjo's cold, numerical assessment of the novelty's value.
feedback.incorrect_en: 買い物 is just 'shopping' and doesn't describe a gaze. 見送り means 'seeing off', unrelated to examination.

prompt.prompt_jp: このペーパーレス化の時代に… ここまで___とは
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adjective Enjo uses to criticize how out of step the company is.

feedback.correct_en: 遅れている ('behind the times') directly critiques the company for lagging the paperless trend — exactly Enjo's complaint.
feedback.incorrect_en: 進んでる ('advanced') is the opposite of his point. 冷たい ('cold') doesn't fit a critique about modernization.

prompt.prompt_jp: そのデータが___かと
prompt.prompt_en: Takakura answers Enjo's question tersely. Pick the word meaning 'everything/all there is'.

feedback.correct_en: データが全て ('the data is everything/the data speaks for itself') captures Takakura's number-only stance perfectly, and it's a natural compact business reply.
feedback.incorrect_en: 少し ('a little') would mean 'the data is a little…', which is incomplete and doesn't match the firm tone. 初め ('beginning') doesn't make sense here.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子がノベルティを渡しながら
prompt.prompt_jp: 恐らく これで ___かと思われますので
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the loan-word Sanako uses to describe balancing out the give/take with Taiyo.

feedback.correct_en: イーブン ('even') is the running motif of this chapter — Sanako wants her relationship with Taiyo to balance out. She reuses the English loan to signal the accounting-style equivalence.
feedback.incorrect_en: ペンディング ('pending') is used for the novelty project, not for interpersonal balance. ノベルティ is the item itself, not a state.

prompt.prompt_jp: ___になっちゃったの ノベルティ
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the loanword meaning 'put on hold' used in business settings.

feedback.correct_en: ペンディング is business-speak for 'pending/on hold' — exactly what happened to the novelty production.
feedback.incorrect_en: オーディション is 'audition' (unrelated). モニター here would mean a product tester, not a status.

contrast_examples.jp: 企画がペンディングになる。
contrast_examples.en: The project is put on hold.

prompt.prompt_jp: ここで中止したら 単なる___じゃないですか！
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word meaning 'pure loss/complete waste' in Kiriha's argument.

feedback.correct_en: 丸損 means 'pure loss' — if you stop after already spending money on samples, you lose all of it with nothing to show. Fits her outrage.
feedback.incorrect_en: 丸得 would mean 'pure gain', the opposite. 中古 means 'secondhand', unrelated.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が真夕のサンプルを断る
prompt.prompt_jp: ___しておきます
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the polite phrase Sanako uses to decline the novelty bag.

feedback.correct_en: 遠慮しておきます is the standard polite refusal ('I'll pass/decline'). It softens 'no' into something diplomatic — very Sanako.
feedback.incorrect_en: 失礼しておきます isn't idiomatic as a refusal. 安心しておきます would mean 'I'll feel reassured', which doesn't fit declining a gift.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が太陽に自分の気持ちを伝える
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Sanako expressing her wish to stay balanced with Taiyo?

choices.text: イーブンでいたいんです あなたとは いつでも
イーブンにしたいんです あなたを いつでも
イーブンがいたいんです あなたと いつでも

feedback.correct_en: イーブンでいる ('stay in an even state') with で+いる is the natural pattern for maintaining a state. The postposed 'あなたとは' adds Sanako's reflective tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'あなたを イーブンにしたい' makes Taiyo the object you adjust, which is odd and controlling. The が version is ungrammatical.

prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'I don't have the right to forbid him'?

choices.text: 私が 禁止する権利ないよ
権利ないよ 私を 禁止する
禁止する 権利が私ない

feedback.correct_en: The original word order — relative clause 禁止する modifying 権利, with 私が as the subject of 禁止する — is natural and compact. Casual drop of が before ない is normal in spoken Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b scrambles the modifier after the head, which Japanese doesn't allow. Option c breaks the relative clause structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 文句を言う権利はない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't have the right to complain.

contrast_examples.jp: やめさせる権利がない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't have the right to stop (him).

prompt.context_jp: 田倉の達観したコメント
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing captures Takakura's 'you can only move number-driven people with numbers' observation most naturally?

choices.text: 数字で動く人間は 数字でしか動かせない
数字で動く人間を 数字しか動かせる
数字が動く人間は 数字でだけ動かせる

feedback.correct_en: 〜しか…ない is the standard 'only' construction. Pairing 数字で (means) with 動かせない (can't move) gives a crisp proverb-like line that fits Takakura's style.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b drops ない from しか, breaking the pattern. Option c says 'numbers that move' (数字が動く), which doesn't describe the people — it misassigns the subject.

contrast_examples.en: You can only pay in cash.

prompt.context_jp: 太陽が照れながら言う
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is the natural way for Taiyo to say 'if you're happy, that makes me happy'?

choices.text: 沙名子さんが喜んでくれれば 俺も うれしくなるから
沙名子さんは喜んでくれれば 俺が うれしくなるから
沙名子さんを喜んでくれれば 俺に うれしくなるから

feedback.correct_en: In a 〜ば conditional clause, the subject typically takes が, and the くれる shows the action is a favor done for Taiyo. 俺も naturally contrasts/parallels him with her.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b incorrectly puts は inside the ば-clause subject slot. Option c mangles the particles — you can't 喜ぶ someone with を here.

contrast_examples.en: If you laugh, I laugh too.

prompt.context_jp: 真夕のアレッサンドロ愛
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which way of expressing 'getting back many times over' fits Mayu's enthusiastic speech?

choices.text: 何十倍にして 返してもらってるんです
何十倍を 返してあげてるんです
何十倍で 返しているんです

feedback.correct_en: 返してもらう ('have (someone) return (it) to me') with 〜にして ('making it into X times') is the natural idiom for 'I get it back many times over'. The もらう direction matches Mayu as the beneficiary.
feedback.incorrect_en: 返してあげる reverses the direction — it would mean she's giving back to him. Option c with で sounds flat and misses the 'turning into' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 倍にして返してもらう。
倍にして返してあげる。
